query: For an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy in its uniform, fine lamellar state, whose strength and plasticity remain below industrial application requirements, what single intervention could improve performance for fasteners exposed to extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive conditions? State the proposed intervention, mechanism, predicted outcome relative to the starting alloy, applicable operating and test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit falsification criteria.

generation.hypothesis: A controlled aging heat treatment that induces the formation of nanoscale precipitates along the lamellar interfaces in the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA will enhance both its strength and plasticity, making it better suited for fastener applications under extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading including room‐temperature creep, and corrosive environments.
generation.material_initial_state: Uniform, fine lamellar microstructure of the as-cast or solution-treated AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy that currently exhibits suboptimal strength and ductility.
generation.intervention: Apply a single post-solidification thermal aging process, for example, holding the alloy at approximately 450°C for about 6 hours in an inert (argon) atmosphere followed by controlled cooling. This treatment is intended to trigger precipitation of nanoscale secondary phases (e.g., B2-type precipitates) along the lamellar interfaces.
generation.conditions: Aging treatment performed at 450°C for 6 hours in an inert atmosphere, followed by air cooling. The treated samples would then be evaluated for mechanical properties at room temperature (tensile tests, creep tests under constant load), for resistance to thermal cycling (e.g., from -40°C to 150°C), and for corrosion resistance in a simulated corrosive environment.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of uniformly distributed nanoscale precipitates along the lamellar interfaces, which serve as obstacles to dislocation motion and contribute to the strengthening of the matrix.
generation.mechanism: Precipitation hardening: the thermal aging results in the formation of fine secondary phase particles which impede dislocation motion, thereby improving yield strength. Simultaneously, the refined microstructure helps to relieve stress concentration and improve ductility, while maintaining phase boundary integrity under long-term mechanical loads, creep, and corrosive conditions.
generation.predicted_outcome: A noticeable increase in yield strength and improved ductility, leading to better performance in terms of mechanical load resistance, decreased room-temperature creep rate, and enhanced corrosion resistance compared to the as-cast/solution-treated fine lamellar state.
generation.baseline: The starting state is the uniform, fine lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 HEA without any post-solidification aging treatment, characterized by insufficient strength and plasticity for industrial fastener applications.
generation.boundary: The aging treatment is expected to be effective when performed under controlled conditions (approximately 450°C for 6 hours) and may not yield the desired improvements if the temperature or duration is significantly altered. The long-term stability of the precipitates under continuous thermal cycling and prolonged creep conditions remains an uncertainty.
generation.uncertainty: The exact aging parameters (temperature and time) for optimal precipitate formation may require further optimization, and there is some uncertainty about the long-term stability of the precipitates under service conditions with repeated temperature fluctuations and extended mechanical loading.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two groups of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 HEA samples: one group receives the controlled aging treatment (450°C for 6 hours in argon, followed by controlled cooling) and the other group serves as the untreated control. Subject both groups to a series of tests including room-temperature tensile and creep tests, thermal cycling from -40°C to 150°C, and corrosion tests in a simulated corrosive medium. Additionally, carry out microstructural analysis using SEM/TEM to verify the presence and distribution of nanoscale precipitates.
measurements: Tensile yield strength and ultimate tensile strength
Creep strain over a fixed duration under constant load
Electrochemical corrosion parameters (e.g., corrosion current density, open circuit potential)
Microstructural features (precipitate size, volume fraction, and distribution)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the aged samples do not demonstrate a statistically significant improvement (for example, less than a 20% enhancement in yield strength and corresponding improvements in ductility and creep resistance) relative to the control group, or if microstructural analysis shows no clear formation of nanoscale precipitates, then the hypothesis will be considered falsified.
